summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems for fracture detection perform strongly in controlled settings, but prospective real-world evidence is limited. In a three-month deployment in one emergency department, thirteen radiographers in a radiographer-led screening programme independently interpreted 2496 consecutive musculoskeletal examinations (one radiographer per examination), reviewed output from a commercial deep-learning system, then recorded a final decision, giving 2496 paired reads against a radiologist reference standard. Standalone AI sensitivity was 75.6%, falling to 46.2% for subtle fractures, below the radiographers’ baseline sensitivity of 91.6%. Radiographers’ baseline accuracy was high (97.6%; specificity 99.0%) and improved modestly with AI assistance (98.0%; exact McNemar p = 0.0064). With AI assistance, radiographers corrected 11 errors and introduced 1, a net gain of 10 cases. Subgroup gains were directionally consistent but not significant after correction. Radiographers changed their decision in only 11 of 729 discordant cases, and most negative interactions were correct AI recommendations not adopted. No or incomplete AI output was returned for 8.8% of acquired examinations. AI assistance delivered a small, selective benefit arising from complementary rather than superior algorithmic performance. Operational reliability proved as consequential as diagnostic accuracy, and behavioural inferences rest on few events. Downstream clinical outcomes were not measured.
title: Radiographer fracture detection with and without AI assistance in prospective emergency department use

summary: Fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA) is the gold standard for diagnosing retinal vascular diseases. However, interpretable artificial intelligence (AI) systems for FFA image analysis that align with clinicians’ reasoning processes and real-world diagnostic workflows remain scarce. In this study, we introduce an interpretable graph reasoning framework, FFA-RGNet, that explicitly models the temporal patterns of fine-grained lesions across imaging phases and anatomical locations for disease diagnosis from sequential FFA images. FFA-RGNet was trained and validated on a large, fine-grained, multi-center dataset consisting of 25,312 FFA images from 2651 patients. FFA-RGNet outperformed nine baseline models on the internal test set, achieving an F1-score of 95.38% (95% CI: 92.24%–97.88%), and demonstrated consistent performance across multi-center and prospective validation datasets. Its diagnostic performance not only surpassed that of ophthalmologists, residents and ophthalmology students, but also improved their diagnostic F1-score by 7.48% to 14.11% when used as an assistive tool. Comprehensive inference analysis further revealed its superior ability to correctly recognize fine-grained semantic entities, and to learn stable, disease-specific graph reasoning patterns aligned with clinical knowledge. These results suggest that FFA-RGNet enables accurate diagnosis with interpretable reasoning progresses, highlighting its strong potential as a reliable AI system for FFA interpretation and clinical decision support.
title: An interpretable graph reasoning framework for enhanced diagnosis in fundus fluorescein angiography

summary: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into clinical medical imaging has advanced diagnostics but also poses challenges in maintaining long-term reliability as input data change. To address this, we present MMC+, a modular framework for scalable drift monitoring that builds on our CheXstray framework for real-time drift detection using multi-modal data concordance (MMC). MMC+ provides a flexible architecture that enables cost-effective continuous performance monitoring in real-world healthcare settings. The framework’s capabilities include aggregating information from multiple data streams using statistical tests or distance metrics, leveraging foundation model embeddings to remove the need for site-specific encoder training, and quantifying uncertainty to better communicate drift significance. Validated with data from Massachusetts General Hospital during the COVID-19 pandemic, MMC+ effectively detects significant data shifts that correlate with performance changes and indicates when AI systems may deviate from acceptable performance bounds. The code for MMC+ is publicly available (Link: https://github.com/FJDorfner/MedImaging-ModelDriftMonitoring/tree/MMC_plus), promoting broader adoption of AI solutions in clinical settings. Our framework significantly advances drift detection while promoting transparency and collaboration in clinical AI research.
title: Scalable drift monitoring in medical imaging AI

summary: Digital therapeutics offer promising solutions for frozen shoulder rehabilitation. This single-center, assessor-blinded, randomized controlled pilot trial compared an AI-based digital therapeutic application (ANAPA ME) with YouTube-based home exercises in 18 patients with frozen shoulder. Following baseline assessments, patients were allocated to the digital therapeutics (DTx) or conventional rehabilitation (CON) group, received a single ultrasound-guided intra-articular corticosteroid injection, and completed a 12-week exercise program. Assessments at weeks 0, 2, 4, 8, and 12 included passive range of motion (ROM), Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Constant Shoulder Score (CSS), Shoulder Pain and Disability Index (SPADI), and EuroQol-5 Dimension-5 Level (EQ-5D-5L). At 12 weeks, the DTx group achieved significantly greater side external rotation ROM (p = 0.04) and improvement from baseline (p = 0.042). EQ-5D-5L showed a significant group × time interaction (p = 0.048), with greater improvement from baseline in the DTx group (p = 0.013). No significant between-group differences were observed in VAS, SPADI, or CSS. These findings suggest that AI-based digital therapeutics may offer preliminary advantages in side external rotation ROM and health-related quality of life over conventional video-based exercises, though confirmation in larger trials is needed. This trial was registered with the Clinical Research Information Service, Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (registration number: PRE20250113-001) on January 13, 2025.
title: Mobile application-based digital therapeutics for frozen shoulder rehabilitation: a single-center, randomized controlled pilot study

summary: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes may reduce documentation burden, but little is known about their adoption during enterprise-scale ambulatory rollout. We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of 2901 ambulatory clinicians at an integrated academic health system using linked electronic health record and vendor usage data from December 2024 through May 2025. Clinician adoption was defined as any use during the study period, and monthly visit-level uptake as the proportion of eligible ambulatory visits in which the ambient AI scribe was used. Adoption and uptake varied substantially across practice settings, specialties, and clinician types. Clinician-level adoption was highest in community internal medicine (67%), community general pediatrics (69%), and academic neurology (53%), and lowest in academic general surgery (16%), obstetrics and gynecology (18%), and psychiatry (19%). Community attending physicians and advanced practice providers showed marked increases in median visit-level uptake, reaching approximately 80%-90% in some groups by May 2025. Distinct longitudinal patterns included slow and steady adoption, early use followed by discontinuation, transient use, and late adoption. These findings suggest that implementation support and evaluation strategies should be tailored to local practice context rather than applied uniformly across a health system.
title: Systemwide adoption patterns of ambient AI scribe technology in an integrated academic health system

summary: Clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) guides-biopsy and treatment decisions, yet its non-invasive diagnosis remains challenging. The incremental value of PSMA PET/CT beyond multiparametric MRI (mpMRI), and the optimal strategy for multimodal fusion, remain unclear. We established a real-world, multicentre benchmark using 527 patients from three hospitals with fully paired PSMA PET, CT, T2-weighted MRI, and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), together with pathology-confirmed biopsy labels. Models were developed in one centre (n = 363) and independently evaluated in two external centres (n = 164). We compared frozen pretrained encoders, fine-tuned 2D and 3D CNN and Vision Transformer models, three fusion strategies, and an interpretable cross-modal Transformer. PSMA PET provided the greatest incremental value, with its removal producing the largest AUC reduction internally (−0.077) and externally (−0.055), supported by the highest attention attribution (αPET = 0.45). PSMA PET/CT also outperformed mpMRI externally (AUC 0.753 vs. 0.653). DWI was the principal source of domain shift, as its exclusion improved external AUC by 0.079 amid inter-centre b-value heterogeneity. Intermediate fusion performed most consistently internally, whereas late fusion and pretrained 2D models generalised better externally. This benchmark supports robust, non-invasive csPCa diagnosis by identifying modalities and fusion strategies that generalise reliably across institutions.
title: Multicentre benchmark of PSMA PET/CT and mpMRI fusion for non-invasive clinically significant prostate cancer diagnosis

summary: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive brain tumor with poor prognosis and limited treatment options. Chimeric antigen receptor T cell (CAR-T) therapy has emerged as a promising immunotherapy for GBM. However, unlike conventional drugs, CAR-T cells are living therapeutics that exhibit non-linear pharmacokinetics, expansion, and complex tissue trafficking, making conventional animal-to-human dose extrapolation unreliable. Furthermore, species-specific differences and the vasculature limit the translational relevance of preclinical models. To address these challenges, we developed GliaDose, a hybrid framework that integrates physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling with a vascularized glioblastoma-on-a-chip (GoC) platform to support quantitative first-in-human dose (FIHD) prediction for CAR-T therapy. The PBPK model was parameterized exclusively with human physiological data and incorporates a brain-tumor compartment to explicitly capture CAR-T transport across the vasculature. Complementarily, the GoC platform recapitulates key features of the GBM microenvironment, including three-dimensional tumor architecture, extracellular matrix, and perfusable human vascular networks, enabling assessment of CAR-T transmigration under flow conditions. Integration of GoC-derived efficacy data into the PBPK framework enabled quantitative dose–response predictions and identified vascular barriers as critical determinants of CAR-T tumor access. GliaDose provides a human-relevant, mechanistic alternative to animal-based dose selection and may improve FIHD prediction and personalized CAR-T therapy for GBM.
title: GliaDose: An alternative approach for clinical CAR-T dose prediction via PBPK–glioblastoma-on-a-chip integration

summary: Adolescent major depressive disorder is a highly prevalent and debilitating condition, yet objective and generalizable neurofunctional signatures remain elusive. Existing neuroimaging approaches largely rely on resting-state fMRI, or controlled tasks often lack ecological validity and generalizable signatures of depression-related neural dysfunctions. This study proposes a Visual–Affective Decoding (VAD) framework integrating cross-subject visual and affective decoding from whole-brain fMRI acquired during naturalistic movie viewing. A dual-pathway anomaly detection model trained exclusively on healthy controls establishes normative brain function and identifies MDD through deviations from this norm. In 200 adolescents (112 MDD, 88 HC), VAD achieved an AUC of 0.87, 95.56% sensitivity, 83.89% accuracy, and 72.22% specificity. Using the same anomaly threshold, it generalized to an independent external adolescent cohort (70 MDD, 68 HC), achieving an AUC of 0.81 with an accuracy of 75.36%, supporting its cross-site generalizability. VAD further revealed interpretable neurofunctional signatures, including blunted emotional reactivity, attenuated visual representation, and affective patterns consistent with emotional rumination. Region-level contribution analyses identified dissociable visual- and affective-sensitive cortical regions, consistent with dysfunctions in visual, default-mode, salience, and higher-order associative networks. These findings demonstrate that VAD provides objective, interpretable, and generalizable neurofunctional signatures for adolescent depression diagnosis and clinically relevant biomarker development.
title: Visual-affective decoding enhances neurofunctional objective and generalizable signatures in unseen adolescent depression diagnosis
